intro_html: Cochinita pibil comes from the Yucatan, where it was traditionally wrapped in banana leaves and buried in a pit oven called a pib. The color and the earthy flavor come from achiote, a brick red paste of annatto seed and spice, cut with sour orange. A slow cooker gets you remarkably close to the real thing for eight hours of doing nothing. Pickled red onion on top is not optional. It is half the dish.
cost_closing_html: About $1.34 a bowl, which makes this the cheapest recipe in this entire batch. A block of achiote paste costs a few dollars, lasts through several batches, and does flavor work you cannot buy any other way.
shop_smart: Achiote paste is the whole flavor and it is cheap. Look for the small red brick in the Hispanic aisle. One block seasons this batch and several more after it, so the per serving cost is tiny.
Orange juice, vinegar and lime stand in for sour orange. Real sour orange is hard to find outside a Latin market. This combination is what every cook in the States uses and it costs pennies.
Pickle the red onion yourself. Sliced thin, covered in lime juice and salt for 30 minutes, and you have the same bright pink topping the restaurant charges extra for.
Pork shoulder plus a slow cooker is the value play. The cheapest cut in the case becomes the best texture on the plate, and the machine does the work while you are somewhere else.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the achiote paste with the orange juice, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper until it is a smooth brick red marinade.
Cut the pork shoulder into large chunks, coat every piece in the marinade, and let it sit at least an hour or overnight in the fridge.
Put the pork and all the marinade in the slow cooker with the beef broth and cook on low for 8 hours, until it falls apart under a fork.
Slice the red onion paper thin, cover it in the lime juice with a pinch of salt, and let it sit at room temperature until it turns pink.
Shred the pork right in the cooking liquid so it soaks the sauce back up. Do not drain it, that red liquid is the whole point.
Cook the rice per the package and warm the tortillas just before you assemble.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice across your 14 containers, then set your mixing pot of shredded pork and its juices on the scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight over the rice. Top each with the pickled onion and pack the tortillas alongside. Every bowl lands near 571 calories with 29 grams of protein.

head.description: Achiote and citrus marinated pork shoulder slow cooked eight hours, shredded over rice with pickled red onion. A 14 serving cochinita pibil for meal prep.
head.keywords: cochinita pibil, slow cooker pork, achiote pork recipe, yucatan food, pork rice bowls, budget meal prep
steps: Whisk the achiote paste with orange juice, vinegar and spices into a marinade.
Coat the cubed pork shoulder and marinate at least an hour.
Slow cook the pork with the marinade and beef broth on low for 8 hours.
Pickle thin sliced red onion in lime juice and salt.
Shred the pork in its juices and serve over rice with pickled onion and warm tortillas.
